source.title: When Are Sparse Feature Interventions Actually Localized? Matched Evaluation for SAE-Based Safety Control

page_placements.theme: SAE and dictionary features as causal control units (not neurons)

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests SAE-feature interventions for safety control, not neuron-pole job counts, neuron explanations, or attribution graphs. Its findings concern a related idea of localized internal interventions but do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for SAE-feature ablation and steering, not for neurons or neuron explanations. Those findings are recorded as related but not covered by a claim version. No results cited from other work are included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares SAE-feature ablation and steering with dense refusal-direction steering for safety control in Gemma-2 and Llama-3.1 models. It never audits neuron poles, explains or scores individual neurons, reanalyses InceptionV1, or builds neuron attribution graphs. Neurons and superposition appear only as background motivation for SAEs, and neither original source is cited. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Against same-layer and decoder-span baselines on Gemma-2-9B, the SAE advantage reverses. Against all-layer dense steering it remains large on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-27B. The paraphrase should add that on 2B the SAE recipe collapses capability and its jailbreaks are largely single-judge inflation. It should also add that for refusal injection dense steering is the more capability-preserving choice. The authors call perturbation a locality proxy, not causal proof.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates inference-time SAE feature ablation and activation steering for safety behavior, rather than auditing neuron explanations or constructing attribution graphs.
record.method_sensitivity: The comparison changes with dense-baseline matching (all-layer versus same-layer or decoder-span projected); model scale and architecture; intervention direction; feature count; and judge choice. The 2B SAE judge discrepancy is not seen in the Llama run using the same prompt source.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-9B, SAE ablation's matched-perturbation advantage over all-layer dense steering (+0.094 to +0.104) reverses against same-layer and decoder-span-projected dense baselines (down to −0.286 and −0.204). The reversal holds under a second judge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent localization advantages of SAE-feature safety interventions depend on whether the dense baseline matches the intervention surface and basis.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE ablation beats all-layer dense steering on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-27B. On Gemma-2-2B it collapses MMLU and GSM8K, and its jailbreak signal is not corroborated by a second judge (κ=0.01).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature intervention quality varies with model scale and architecture, and single-judge metrics can inflate small-model results.

fits_no_version.finding: All 30 audited high-k unsafe-incoherent SAE outputs were degenerate. Single-feature ablations raised true jailbreak to at most 0.04.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal control via SAE features is distributed over a medium-k head, and high-k ablation outputs need coherence gating.

record.code_released: not publicly released; authors say materials are available on request until public release
record.problems: The study measures SAE-feature intervention effects, not neuron interpretability or neuron-based circuits. Its Gemma-2-27B comparison uses three seeds and 4-bit weights, with capability benchmarks omitted because the baseline is near floor. The human audit is targeted and single-annotator. Llama and 27B comparisons use an all-layer dense baseline rather than the surface-matched baselines tested on 9B.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results were omitted from the selected related findings; results not pertaining to SAE feature intervention or its safety evaluation were not recorded.

record.verdict_notes: Unrelated to the neurons_already_clean claim. The paper concerns SAE features, not neurons, and does not cite either original source. 'discusses' is generous: the closest contact is a background sentence that SAEs are motivated by superposition and aim to be more interpretable than neurons. Unrecorded results (Table 3 matched-TE ties, Table 6 layer scan, Table 10 retain set, Table 12 injection direction) also bear on no version.
